agent: frontier-loaders: the four most-called unnamed functions left, all reached from *::LoadKey
question: 0x669550, 0x67B540, 0x4CDA0 and 0x5C7D60 - what each one is, its signature and convention read off the ret and the call sites, and a name or a statement that it cannot be named

addresses.name: TokenToFixedPoint
addresses.comment:
Turns a `CToken`'s text into the engine's thousandths fixed point: `*out = atoi(text) * 1000 + fraction`, where `fraction` is the digits after the first `.` read as a number and then padded with zeros to exactly three places - `1.5` gives 1500, `1.25` gives 1250, `2` gives 2000, and a token with no `.` at all gives a fraction of 0. The sign comes from `text[0]`: when it is `-` and `atoi` returned 0 the fraction is negated anyway, so `-0.5` comes out -500.

The `imul 1000` / `__allmul(x,1000)` / `__alldiv(x,1000000)` round trip in the middle is a 64 bit overflow guard on a fraction with more than three digits, not a second scaling - `lea edx,[eax+0x189373]; cmp edx,0x39580D` picks the 32 bit path only when `eax*1000` cannot overflow, and both paths hand the same fraction back. The fast path's `0x431BDE83` with `sar edx,0x12` is the standard divide-by-1000000 magic (2^50/10^6 = 1125899906.8).

**188 direct call sites, all loaders**, and the argument is `parse + 0x228` (`CParseContext::value`, the CToken) at every one looked at. It takes the token, not the context, so it reports nothing: a token that is not a number simply gives 0. It answers `out` in eax so the caller can read the value straight back - `call; mov eax,[eax]; mov [ebx+0xC4],eax` at 0x4CDE8B, and `call; movd xmm0,[eax]; cvtdq2ps; divsd [0x160A300]` (1000.0) at 0x4B1F93, which is the float the loader actually wanted.
addresses.evidence: Read instruction by instruction from 0xA69550 to the `ret 8`, with every constant checked: 0x3E8 = 1000, 0xF4240 = 1000000, 0x2E = '.', 0x30 = '0', 0x2D = '-', and 0x160A300 (the divisor at the 0x4B1F93 call site) holds the double 1000.0. `ret 8` with two stack arguments and no `add esp` at any call site inspected makes it __stdcall; the two callees are already named `atoi`, `__allmul` and `__alldiv` in project.json. Wrong if: the `1000` were a scale rather than a guard (it is not - the fast and slow paths are algebraically identical, `frac*1000*1000/1000000`), or if a call site tested the return as a status rather than dereferencing it (0x4CDE8B and 0x4B1F93 both dereference; a site that does `test eax,eax` after this call would show the reading wrong).

addresses.name: ParseFixedPoint
addresses.comment:
The fixed point reader of the `*::LoadKey` family, beside `ParseInt` (0x67B470), `ParseBool` and `ParseString`: `*out` gets the value token as thousandths. Both arguments are in registers, so there is nothing on the stack and the function ends in a bare `ret`.

It takes one of two readings, decided by the tokenizer's virtual slot 2 - `mov ecx,[parse+0x1C]; mov eax,[ecx]; call [eax+8]`, on the field project.json already calls `CParseContext::tokenizer`. That slot is `_purecall` in the tokenizer base (vftable 0x15FD1F0, slots 1 and 2 both 0xB961D5) and a compile time constant in each subclass, so it is a kind flag, not a computation: the tokenizer used everywhere for files (vftable 0x15FD1FC, 78 construction sites) answers **false** through `xor al,al; ret` at 0x192360, and the rarer one (vftable 0x15FD208, 4 sites, all reached from the 0xB3xxxx network module) answers **true** through `mov al,1; ret` at 0x692590.

True takes the text as already scaled - `sscanf(parse->value.text, "%i", out)` straight into `*out`. False sends `&parse->value` to 0x6696A0, which is the checked form of `TokenToFixedPoint`: `sscanf("%i")` for the whole part, `strstr(text, ".")` for a fraction, the first three fraction digits zero-padded, and the whole thing multiplied by 1000 - so the `1.5` a script file writes becomes 1500. Either reading failing ends in `ReportParseError(parse@ESI)`, which esi already holds.

**76 direct call sites**, the switch arm shape being `mov eax,[ebp+8]; lea edi,[<field>]; call` with the caller's `ret 8` right after (0x414FB4, 0x4CD030).
addresses.evidence: The body and both branches read at 0xA7B540; the argument registers read off three call sites (0x414FB4, 0x414FC4, 0x4CD030) which all set eax = the `CParseContext*` the LoadKey received and edi = a `lea` of the destination field, and pass nothing on the stack - matching the bare `ret`. The slot 2 bodies were reached by dumping the three 3-slot tables at 0x15FD1F0/0x15FD1FC/0x15FD208 and disassembling each: 0xB961D5 is `_purecall` (it loads 0xD2B040 and calls `_amsg_exit(0x19)`), 0x192360 is `xor al,al; ret`, 0x692590 is `mov al,1; ret`. Wrong if: the two register arguments were the other way round (they are not - `[edi]` is written and `[esi+0x22C]` is read as text), or if the file/network reading of the two subclasses is backwards. That last part is **inference** from where the constructors are called (0xA6A800's callers are 0xA8A512 and five sites in 0xB35xxx-0xB3Axxx, the network module project.json already identifies in `CParseContext::error_handler`); it does not affect the name, because both branches put a thousandths value in `*out`.

addresses.name: Date_SetFromString
addresses.signature: void __stdcall Date_SetFromString(int* date@ESI, const char* text)
addresses.comment:
Sets a date tick from the text `year.month.day.hour`, in place, joining `Date_Year`, `Date_DayOfYear`, `Date_DayOfMonth` and `Date_DayOfWeek` as the writing half of that family. **782 direct call sites**, the most-called unnamed function in the image after the parse helpers, and the text handed to it is `parse + 0x22C` (`CParseContext::value.text`) at every site inspected.

It is `sscanf(text, "%d.%d.%d.%d", &year, &month, &day, &hour)`, then month and day are decremented to 0 based, then the tick is rebuilt on the epoch `CLASSES.md` records: `tick = 24 * sign(year) * (365*|year| + dayOfYear(old tick)) + 43800000 + hourOfDay(old tick)`, where 0x29C55C0 = 43800000 and 0x538AB8*8 is the same number. The month is then added by 0x4C420 and the day of the month by 0x4C360 - both walk the month length table at rva 0x1313294 - and finally the hour of day is replaced by the parsed one. Callers hand it a date holding exactly the epoch (`mov [esp+0x64],0x29C55C0; lea esi,[esp+0x64]` at 0x4CE4A2), so the old day-of-year and hour-of-day it preserves are both zero and the result is exactly the date in the string.

**The sscanf return is never tested.** A string that is not a date leaves year 0 and, because the decrements are unconditional, month -1 and day -1, so the tick walks backwards off the epoch and nothing is reported - the same silence `FINDINGS-...` records for unknown keys.
addresses.evidence: Read from 0x44CDA0 to the `ret 4`. The format string at 0x15BB3F8 is `%d.%d.%d.%d` and the push order fixes which local is which (year at ebp-0xC, month at ebp-4, day at ebp-8, hour at ebp-0x10). The arithmetic constants were each computed out: 0xFD63AA40 = -43800000, 0x29C55C0 = 43800000, 8*0x538AB8 = 43800000, 0x16D = 365, the divisor 24, and the double at 0x160A550 = 365.0 - all agreeing with the tick epoch CLASSES.md:90 already records. The register argument is read off three call sites (0x4CE4AA, 0x5E275B, 0x42F649), each of which sets esi (a `lea` of a 4 byte date, once initialised to the epoch) and pushes exactly the text, matching `ret 4`. The two callees 0x4C420 and 0x4C360 index rva 0x1313294, the month length table FINDINGS-autosave.md:78 already identified. Wrong if: the four fields were in a different order (the decrement of exactly the 2nd and 3rd, and the 1st being multiplied by 365, pin year/month/day), or if a caller passed the date in a register other than esi - a call site that sets esi to something else before the call would show it.

addresses.name: StringHashFind
addresses.comment:
Looks a name up in the engine's own string hash table and answers the stored pointer, or null. **206 direct call sites.**

The table is `{int count; unsigned bucketCount; void** buckets;}` at +0/+4/+8 and a node is `{void* value; Node* next;}`. The hash is the engine's string hash, `h = (h + c) * 61` over the length of the key (`imul eax,eax,0x3D`, the same three bytes inlined at 23 places in the image), reduced by `div [table+4]`. Each node in the bucket is compared by taking `value + 8` as an `Hoi3CString` and running the 4-bytes-at-a-time compare at 0x15F70 over `min(keylen, storedlen)` characters, with the lengths broken as the tie - so **the key is a member of the stored object, at +8**, and nothing is copied into the table.

That +8 is what fixes this instantiation of what is otherwise a template body: the insert half at 0x5C87C0 is the same table and the same hash with the key at value+4. The table itself is a member of whatever owns it (`esi+0x10` of a global at 0x4CDCE7, `vf[0x44]() + 0x6BCF0` at 0x406B5A), and the value is used as a polymorphic object straight afterwards (`mov edx,[eax]; mov ecx,eax; call [edx+0x48]`), so this is the by-name index the loaders go through when a script names a thing.

No class on the name deliberately: the body is shared by several owners, it is in no virtual table, and which class the values belong to is not settled here.
addresses.evidence: Read from 0x9C7D60 to both `ret 4` exits, and the SSO test `cmp [key+0x14],0x10` with the length at +0x10 is the `Hoi3CString` layout project.json already records (0x10 length, 0x14 capacity). The convention is read off two call sites: 0x4CDCE7 (`mov eax,esi; add eax,0x10`, one push) and 0x406B5A (`call [eax+0x44]; add eax,0x6BCF0`, one push), both matching `ret 4` with the table in eax. The `imul eax,eax,0x3D` hash was scanned for across .text: 23 sites, of which 0x9C87E8 is the insert at 0x5C87C0 with the same `div [this+4]`, `[this+8]` bucket array and `{value,next}` node, which is what makes the container reading checkable rather than a guess. Wrong if: +8 were not the key - a caller that inserts through 0x5C87C0 into the *same* table would prove the key offsets contradict and mean these are one instantiation rather than two; or if 0x15F70 turned out not to be a comparison (it returns the first differing byte difference, so it is). Not settled: which class the stored values are, and therefore whether this deserves a `Class::Find` name.

slots_noted: none of the four is in any class's virtual table - `vtable.py --holding` answers 'is in no class's virtual table' for all of 0x44CDA0, 0xA69550, 0xA7B540 and 0x9C7D60.
frontier_notes: 0x6696A0 is the checked form of TokenToFixedPoint - `sscanf("%i")`, `strstr(text, ".")` at 0x15B5C64, the first three fraction digits into a local pre-set to '000', and a *1000 on the whole part - returning false instead of a value when the text is not a number; it is `ret 8`, (CToken* token, int* out), and is worth naming next to the two already here. 0x4C420 and 0x4C360 set the month and the day of the month on a tick from the month length table at rva 0x1313294, both taking the date on the stack and the number in eax. 0x15F70 is a memcmp shaped comparison with a register convention - `(size_t n@stack:4, const void* a@EDX, const void* b@ECX)`, four bytes at a time then bytewise, returning the byte difference - and is probably `std::char_traits<char>::compare` out of line. 0x192360 (`xor al,al; ret`) and 0x692590 (`mov al,1; ret`) are slot 2 of the two tokenizer subclasses; each is a one instruction constant and neither can be named without naming the subclass, which is a table-shaped job for a later wave (the three tables are at 0x15FD1F0, 0x15FD1FC and 0x15FD208, three slots each, and no class in project.json claims them).
